type: is the SCALE_SHRUNK warning a false alarm for a model that standardises its inputs
conclusion: uniformly rescaling a column is exactly a no-op for a model that standardises each input column, so the ratio rule flagged a condition that cannot change any prediction
action: the ratio rule is demoted from a flag to an informational note; it no longer affects the passed field

what_it_corrects.R150: the ratio branch was implemented and its implementation validated, but it measures something unrelated to predictions
what_it_corrects.R151: the ratio threshold is not merely unpicked, it is unanchorable for this model family since there is no behaviour to anchor to

where_it_still_matters: trees on unstandardised inputs, distance-based methods, and anything sensitive to feature scale; the note is retained for those callers to promote if they wish
limits: Proven only for standardised linear models.
At scale zero the delta is 5.6e-07, but a fully zeroed column changes the design matrix rank so it should be reported; the existing CONSTANT_ON_EVAL rule does that.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim.
next_gate: run the same test under a tree; if the tree is also nearly invariant the note can be removed, and if not it should stay as an optional flag
